subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and next steps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.dev>

Subject: Post-call recap: rate limits & overage pricing — next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Alex — good to hear more about Acme's usage patterns. Recap + asks below so we have a single thread for pricing/ops: 

Summary from call:
- Current baseline: ~2M tokens/month (inference tokens).
- Expected growth: ramp to ~10-15M tokens/month over next 6 months (marketing + catalog search).
- Burst pattern: short spikes during campaigns — peak traffic ~3-4x baseline across a few hours, with extreme test bursts we've seen in the logs up to ~10x for <1 hour.
- Primary concern: predictable unit cost and avoiding throttling during campaign bursts.

Asks / next steps for you:
1) Confirm the 10-15M target and typical burst duration (minutes vs hours).
2) Budget target for inference spend (ballpark $/1M tokens you want us to hit). You mentioned finance is reviewing — cc'd Finance Ops.
3) Any procurement cadence/timing constraints (PO lead time, contract approver).

What I attached: acme_weekly_usage.csv — we pulled the last 8 weeks of request counts to model burst shapes. Also attaching our public overage terms (redwood-overage-terms.pdf) for your review.

Quick pricing context so we align expectations before a pricing review: our hosted API has tiered unit pricing and a burst/soft-quota model that permits transient spikes while we process quota increase requests. Typical public (list) rates are higher than committed/contracted rates — we can provide committed-volume pricing once we have a confirmed target $/1M tokens or commitment level.

Propose: a 30-minute follow-up next week with our pricing ops to run a simple unit-economics calc (examples at $/1M tokens) — are you available Tue/Wed?

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.dev | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. Quick answers: 

1) Confirming the 10-15M target within 6 months assuming we roll this into two additional product flows (search + notifications). We could see a steady state of ~12M by month 6.
2) Bursts are usually campaign-driven and last ~1-3 hours. We do get short spikes of a few minutes (load tests) that are higher but those are infrequent.
3) Budget: Finance wants to stay <= $20 / 1M tokens if possible (we're targeting unit economics that keep inference spend under 1.5% of ARR). If committed pricing needs a minimum term, we can consider it — need to see numbers first.

Finance is asking specifically about: quota increase SLAs, burst handling (do you queue vs throttle), and overage pricing (how much above committed rate?). Please include those details in the follow-up.

Also attaching the usage export we ran on our side (acme_payload_summary.pdf) so you can cross-reference.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and numbers

Thanks Alex — super helpful. Below I outlined our standard approaches and a couple of concrete pricing examples so Finance has something to react to. This is preliminary / public-list guidance; committed pricing will be lower and depends on term/commit.

Operational model (how we handle bursts & quota increases):
- Soft quota + burst buffer: hosted accounts have a configurable monthly quota with a short-term burst allowance. Small spikes are absorbed by the buffer and are not billed as quota overages immediately. If sustained over the buffer window, requests are either queued briefly or routed to fallback model variants depending on your latency tolerance.
- Quota increase SLA: for signed/committed customers, standard SLA for quota raises is 24-72 hours depending on region and capacity; for enterprise/dedicated customers we offer contractual response times and reserved capacity to eliminate throttling.
- Overage handling: overages are billed at an overage rate (public list overage = 1.25x list rate; contracted overage can be negotiated). For bursts below a configured threshold we often apply a grace window and do not bill immediately — we reconcile monthly.

Example unit economics scenarios (tokens are inference tokens):
- Public list pricing (hosted, no commit): $25 / 1M tokens (example).
- Committed volume (12M/mo committed, 12-month term): $18 / 1M tokens.
- Dedicated / reserved capacity: $12 / 1M tokens (includes reserved throughput, predictable latency).
- Overage example: if committed rate = $18/1M, public overage multiplier = 1.25x -> overage billed at $22.50 / 1M for transient sustained overages. We can cap or tier overage for long-tail spikes as part of contract.

Given your target of <= $20/1M, a 12M/mo commitment looks like the right starting point — committed pricing would likely get you into the $16-19 range depending on term and whether you want a burst SLA or dedicated pool.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) I'll run a quick model with the attached acme_weekly_usage.csv vs Alex's export to show projected monthly spend across the three pricing tiers (public vs committed vs reserved).
2) Offer: if Acme can commit to 12M/mo for 12 months, we can propose a term that targets $18 / 1M with a capped overage at $22.5 / 1M and a 48-hour quota increase SLA.
3) Pricing ops review call — propose Mon 3/23 10:00am PT or Tue 3/24 11:00am PT. Which works for you and Finance?

Happy to adjust the numbers — want to make sure we put a proposal in front of Finance that meets your target while protecting capacity.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.dev

Subject: INTERNAL: Acme pricing posture / recommended offer (ACME-2026-03)

Looping you both to confirm our recommended commercial. Acme is targeting <= $20 / 1M tokens and expects ~12M/mo by month 6. My suggested starting proposal to team: 
- Commit: 12M tokens/month, 12-month term.
- Price: $18 / 1M tokens committed.
- Overage: $22.5 / 1M (1.25x committed) with monthly reconciliation and an initial 48-hour grace/burst window.
- SLA: 48-hour quota increase SLA for hosted; offer option to upgrade to Dedicated for guaranteed throughput (pricing uplift).

Why this posture: meets their $20 target, gives us predictable committed volume, and keeps margin headroom. If Rafael thinks capacity risk is high, we can push for Dedicated but that likely raises list-equivalent commitment and requires infra approval.

Can you confirm feasibility from capacity/pricing ops? If yes, I'll send a formal proposal and schedule the ops call for Mon/Tue as above.

Thanks —
Marissa
